And for decades, no single drug molecule could fix it—it took a 3-drug combination (Elexacaftor + Tezacaftor + Ivacaftor / Alyftrek) to lock the gate open.

Because a tensegrity truss transmits force only when its equilibrium matrix A leaves exactly ONE coordinated motion (N_floppy = 1) and internal cable prestress (N_self_stress >= 1). Deleting Phe508 injects 10 extra floppy wobble modes (N_floppy = 11); by the Maxwell-Calladine Theorem, one corrector only pins one side of the rim, whereas two independent corrector struts (Tezacaftor + Elexacaftor) plus one potentiator prestress cable (Ivacaftor) collapse the wobble modes back to N_floppy = 2!

stage_1b_winning_discoveries.title: Doob h-Transform Conditional Markov Survival & 55-nt EJC Boundary Law Across All 92 Indexed Class I CFTR Nonsense Alleles (Q2X to Q1423X)
stage_1b_winning_discoveries.governing_law: P^(h)_{e,e+1} = Q_{e,e+1} h(e+1)/h(e) = 1.0 · h(c) = h_0 (1 − γ_SMG6(1 − 0.85 η_shield))^N_EJC(c) · V_Doob(c) = −ln h(c)
stage_1b_winning_discoveries.cool_human_fact: Not all 'stop signs' in the CFTR gene behave the same! Our lab's math verifier indexes 92 distinct Class I nonsense mutations—from Q2X at the 2nd amino acid all the way to Q1423X near the very end at position 1423. Where that stop sign sits along the 27 exons decides whether the cell shreds the mRNA message or spares it!
stage_1b_winning_discoveries.cross_field_analogy: Picture a train (the ribosome) riding across 26 checkpoint gates (Exon-Junction Complexes) to deliver a message. As the train passes each gate, it knocks a red flag down. If a broken track (a nonsense mutation like G542X at Exon 12) stops the train early, 15 red flags are still standing ahead—calling in the wrecking crew (SMG6) to shred the message. But if the stop sign is past the very last gate (like Q1411X or Q1412X in Exon 27), no red flags remain, so the message survives!
